coverage.notes: SEL: ODE's page says the State Board of Education formally adopted Oregon's Transformative SEL Framework and Standards in 2023 (OAR 581-022-2030; ORS 329.045; HB 2166 of 2021). Five K-12 standards (one per domain), each with 3-4 practices (codes like TSEL.K12.SAI.1A); the standards are deliberately not written in grade bands. Portrait of a Graduate: ODE's own September 2022 SB 744 report (PDF page 40) says some Oregon districts have local graduate profiles but 'there is currently not a statewide graduate profile'. ODE's 2026-2028 strategic plan has no mention of a Portrait or Profile of a Graduate. That report is four years old, so reviewer: confirm with ODE that nothing statewide has been started since. A web search summary claimed a 2024-25 report listed Oregon as state-led; I read that report (ERIC ED673550) and it does not mention Oregon, so that claim is unsupported.

frameworks.name: Oregon's Transformative Social and Emotional Learning Framework & Standards
frameworks.issuingBody: Oregon Department of Education / State Board of Education
frameworks.notes: Read from ODE's PDF https://www.oregon.gov/ode/educator-resources/standards/SEL/Documents/Oregon%20TSEL_standards_with_updated%20template_Accessible.pdf (cover: adopted by State Board June 2023, 'version 10'; footers say 'Version 2.0'; file dated June 2026). Items: the 5 standards plus their 18 practices, read from the Standards pages. CASEL competency is set only on the 5 standards: the document says they braid CASEL's five competencies with five focal constructs, and domain names follow CASEL's order; I did not read the Figure 3 graphic, so please confirm. DISCREPANCY: in the current PDF, practice 5A's text is a copy of 4A, but its growth indicators are about curiosity and critical thinking, and the 2023 copy (https://drc.casel.org/content/uploads/sites/3/2024/02/ODE_Oregons-Transformative-SEL-Framework-Standards_FINAL.pdf) words 5A that way. The 5A entry uses that intended wording. Confirm with ODE.

items.title: Self-Awareness & Identity
items.summary: Identify and reflect on one's thoughts, emotions, behaviors, intersectional identity and capabilities across situations.

items.title: Identify and label emotions, thoughts and strengths
items.summary: Name emotions, thoughts, strengths and potential, both personal and cultural.

items.title: Understand the stress response system
items.summary: Understand regulation and dysregulation, and which environments and experiences trigger stress responses.

items.title: Reflect on how emotions and perspectives influence behavior
items.summary: Evaluate how one's emotions, thoughts, values, biases and prejudices shape behavior.

items.title: Analyze intersectional identities and positionality
items.summary: Examine personal and social identities and how they connect to interests, purpose and belonging.

items.title: Self-Management & Agency
items.summary: Use management strategies to build personal and collective agency toward goals and aspirations.

items.title: Manage and express thoughts, emotions, impulses and stressors
items.summary: Handle and express them in ways that affirm one's identity.

items.title: Adapt management strategies to the situation
items.summary: Choose different strategies for different settings while pursuing personal and collective goals and affirming identity.

items.title: Plan, evaluate and achieve goals
items.summary: Plan for, check progress on and reach personal and collective goals and aspirations.

items.title: Develop agency through communication
items.summary: Use verbal, body-language and written communication to make choices and take initiative.

items.title: Social Awareness & Belonging
items.summary: Build social awareness that fosters belonging and helps co-create equitable, thriving communities.

items.title: Understand similarities and differences in identities
items.summary: Show awareness of the similarities and differences that shape personal and collective identities.

items.title: Apply social skills to healthy relationships
items.summary: Use empathy and compassion to build relationships that reach shared goals while affirming identities and perspectives.

items.title: Foster belonging in a diverse community
items.summary: Cultivate acceptance, support and inclusion of others while addressing the impact of systemic injustice.

items.title: Relationship Skills & Collaborative Problem-Solving
items.summary: Build and keep healthy, supportive relationships and work through diverse settings to solve problems together.

items.title: Form authentic relationships
items.summary: Build relationships that support autonomy while growing cultural awareness and empathy through communication.

items.title: Show empathy during teamwork
items.summary: Demonstrate empathy and affirm others' perspectives during teamwork and collaborative problem solving.

items.title: Recognize harm and the need to repair
items.summary: Notice harm to self and others and identify when support, agency and repair practices are needed.

items.title: Restore relationships
items.summary: Repair relationships by engaging, collaborating and affirming cultural and social perspectives.

items.title: Responsible Decision-Making & Curiosity
items.summary: Use curiosity and analysis of oneself and society to make caring choices for personal, social and collective well-being.

items.title: Demonstrate curiosity, open-mindedness and critical thinking
items.summary: Apply curiosity and open-mindedness with critical thinking across situations (intended wording; see framework notes).

items.title: Make informed choices and address injustice
items.summary: Make informed choices and find solutions to personal and social injustices after analyzing information.

items.title: Anticipate and evaluate the impact of choices
items.summary: Anticipate, reflect on and evaluate how one's choices and contributions affect personal, family and community well-being.

alignments.framework: Oregon's Transformative Social and Emotional Learning Framework & Standards
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." The lesson has students recognise when emotions start driving behaviour and choose a response, which is the same skill.
